questions.q: According to the lesson, why is the per-row int8 Weight MSE significantly lower than the per-tensor int8 Weight MSE?
options: Per-row scaling uses a smaller max_int value (7 instead of 127).
The per-tensor scale is dominated by large values in specific rows, which crushes small values in other rows, whereas per-row scaling preserves them.
Per-row int8 requires less memory for storing scales, allowing for higher precision.
Per-tensor quantization uses asymmetric rounding, while per-row uses symmetric rounding.
questions.answer: The per-tensor scale is dominated by large values in specific rows, which crushes small values in other rows, whereas per-row scaling preserves them.
questions.why: The lesson states: 'Why? Because the per-tensor scale was dominated by the large values in Row 1, crushing the small values in Row 0. Per-row scaling preserved them.'

questions.q: In the context of symmetric quantization for int8, what value is used for max_int and why?
options: 127, to avoid the -128 edge case and maintain symmetry.
7, because int8 is a subset of int4.
255, to utilize the full unsigned range.
questions.answer: 127, to avoid the -128 edge case and maintain symmetry.
questions.why: The lesson explicitly states: 'For int8, max_int is 127 (range -128 to 127, but we use 127 for symmetry to avoid the -128 edge case).'

questions.q: What is the primary trade-off described in the 'intuition' section regarding the granularity of quantization scales (per-tensor vs. per-row vs. per-group)?
questions.why: The lesson states: 'This is the core tension of quantization: Granularity vs. Overhead. The more scales you keep... the more accurate you are, but the more memory you spend storing those scales.'

questions.q: According to the lab results, what percentage of bytes are saved when using per-row int8 quantization compared to the baseline?
questions.why: The lab results section lists: 'RESULT per_row_int8_bytes_saved_pct = 62.5'.

questions.q: Why does ComfyUI silently fall back to full precision if a GPU does not support INT8 compute?
options: To prevent the application from crashing.
Because INT8 is always slower than FP16.
To ensure the model weights are not corrupted.
Because the comfy_quant module does not support INT8.
questions.answer: To prevent the application from crashing.
questions.why: The lesson states: '...ComfyUI doesn’t crash; it silently falls back to full precision.'
